title: Minimum Path Sum
prompt: Given an `m x n` grid filled with non-negative numbers, find a path from the top-left to the bottom-right corner that minimizes the sum of all numbers along the path. You may only move either down or right at any point in time.

examples.explanation: The path 1->3->1->1->1 (right, right, down, down) minimizes the sum.
With a single cell, the start and end are the same, so the path sum is just that cell's value.

hints: The cheapest way to reach any cell only depends on the cheapest way to reach the cell above it or the cell to its left.
Define dp[r][c] as the minimum path sum to reach (r, c). The first row and first column can only be reached one way each, by accumulating along the edge.
For interior cells, dp[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(dp[r-1][c], dp[r][c-1]).

solution.approach: This is the classic grid-path DP: dp[r][c] holds the minimum sum to reach cell (r, c) from the top-left. The first row can only be reached by moving right the whole way, so each cell accumulates the running sum from the left; similarly the first column accumulates downward. For any interior cell, the robot arrived either from above or from the left, so dp[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(dp[r-1][c], dp[r][c-1]) — always extending the cheaper of the two possible predecessors. The answer is dp[m-1][n-1]. The grid itself can be updated in place to avoid extra space.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra space (in-place on the input grid)
